<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - LLM4S is a Scala framework/library for building reliable, maintainable LLM-driven applications.  
   - It provides:  
     • A core API for calling language models (LLMConnect).  
     • A tool-calling API and parameter extraction (ToolAPI).  
     • An agent abstraction for multi-step workflows.  
     • A containerized “workspace agent” protocol and runner for secure code execution.  

2. Main components to show in the diagram  
   a. Client / Sample Code  
      – Entry points (e.g. BasicLLMCallingExample, MultiToolExample, ContainerisedWorkspaceDemo)  
   b. LLM4S Core Library (host side)  
      – Agent module  
      – LLMConnect module (with Provider clients: OpenAIClient, AnthropicClient, AzureOpenAIClient)  
      – ToolAPI module (ToolRegistry, SchemaDefinition, SafeParameterExtractor)  
      – Tokenization utilities  
   c. Shared Protocol  
      – WorkspaceAgentInterface (protocol definitions, codecs)  
      – JSON/HTTP/gRPC messages defining file ops & command execution  
   d. Workspace Runner (inside Docker)  
      – RunnerMain, WorkspaceAgentInterfaceImpl  
      – Executes file I/O, shell commands, tool logic in isolation  
   e. External Services  
      – LLM provider endpoints (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)  
      – Docker daemon (for container lifecycle)  

3. Component interactions & data flow  
   1. Sample code calls into the LLM4S API (Agent or direct LLMConnect).  
   2. LLMConnect serializes a Completion request → HTTP/HTTPS → External LLM provider → Response → LLM4S.  
   3. If using tool-calling or workspace agent:  
      • Core library marshals a WorkspaceAgentInterface request (JSON) → pipes/HTTP → Workspace Runner container.  
      • Runner executes the requested operation (read/write file, run command) → returns result.  
   4. The core Agent orchestrates multiple LLM calls, tool calls, and workspace interactions.  

4. Architectural patterns & design principles  
   - Modular separation between:  
     • Core API for LLM calls  
     • Tool-calling logic  
     • Agent orchestration  
     • Security boundary (containerized workspace runner)  
   - Protocol-driven integration (Shared code used on both host and runner)  
   - Cross-compilation support (common vs Scala 2.13 vs Scala 3 source directories)  

5. Diagram construction guidelines  
   a. Draw a boundary box labeled “Host Application” containing:  
      – Client / Sample component  
      – LLM4S Core modules (Agent, LLMConnect, ToolAPI, Shared Protocol)  
   b. Draw a boundary box labeled “Docker Container” containing:  
      – WorkspaceRunner components (RunnerMain, WorkspaceAgentInterfaceImpl)  
   c. Outside these, place “LLM Provider APIs” (OpenAI, Anthropic).  
   d. Use directional arrows:  
      – From Client to Core API (solid)  
      – Core → Provider endpoints (HTTP request/response)  
      – Core → Docker Container (Protocol messages)  
      – Container → Core (Protocol responses)  
   e. Color-code components:  
      – Green for Host-side library modules  
      – Blue for Container-side runner  
      – Orange for External services (LLM providers, Docker daemon)  
   f. Use distinct shapes:  
      – Rectangles for modules/services  
      – Dashed boxes for version-specific source sets (optional detail)  
      – Cylinders for any persisted state (e.g., logs or cached tokens)  

6. Tailoring details to LLM4S  
   - Emphasize the Shared code (protocol definitions) sits on both sides.  
   - Show cross-compilation directories as an annotation near the Host box.  
   - Note the “Workspace Agent Interface” arrow loop for tool-calling and secure execution.  
   - Annotate the LLMConnect block with supported providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure).  

7. Checklist for a clear diagram  
   – Labels for all modules and services  
   – Arrows annotated with data format (JSON, HTTP) and direction  
   – Color legend indicating host modules, container modules, external services  
   – Boundary boxes for Host vs Container  
   – Optional callouts on cross-compilation source structure  

By following these steps you will produce a detailed, accurate system design diagram that captures LLM4S’s architecture: how client code leverages the core library, interacts securely with its containerized workspace runner, and communicates with external LLM providers.  
</explanation>
